meta.title: Master · Part 2 · Open cloze
meta.provenance: Rewritten for B2 on 2 November 2026 (tools/build-master-part2.py): every gap now sits in a short text whose context decides it, fixed phrases are gapped on the grammar word as Part 2 does, eleven collocation items moved to Master · Part 1, and new items added for the words the real papers test most. Built on the October review of the pantry drafts (cloze.js–cloze4.js), whose answer checks are kept. Frequencies are counted from the 312 gaps of 24 past B2 First Part 2 texts (the Use of English Portfolio); a word that is one of several accepted answers counts once for that gap. 14 Nov 2026: six reference items (they, this, it, these pointing back) from the retired Cohesion Tools.

items.s: Mia has always been brilliant ___ anything involving numbers, so nobody was surprised when she chose to study engineering.
items.why: Brilliant / good at something. Good with numbers is also right.

items.s: After months of planning, we are really looking forward ___ finally getting on the plane.
items.why: Look forward to + -ing: to is a preposition here, so the verb takes -ing.

items.s: Daniel arrived forty minutes after the start. He apologised ___ keeping everyone waiting and blamed the traffic.
items.why: Apologise for (doing) something.

items.s: Whether we hold the barbecue in the garden or not will depend ___ the weather on the day.
items.why: Depend on (or upon).

items.s: Although the team lost the final, the coach said she had never been prouder ___ her players.
items.why: Proud of — and prouder of.

items.s: Nobody in the office was surprised ___ the news that Alex had resigned; he had been unhappy for months.
items.why: Surprised at or by.

items.s: We have already missed the last train, so there is no point ___ rushing to the station now.
items.why: There is no point in + -ing.

items.s: Lucy has become increasingly interested ___ Japanese culture since her trip to Kyoto, and she is now learning the language.
items.why: Interested in.

items.s: The airline has still not given passengers a reason ___ the delay, which has left hundreds of them stranded.
items.why: A reason for something.

items.s: Many people who are afraid ___ flying find that the fear disappears once they understand how planes work.
items.why: Afraid of.

items.s: In spite ___ the rain, thousands of fans stayed until the very end of the concert.
items.why: In spite of + noun phrase (despite has no of).

items.s: The final was postponed because ___ the storm, which had flooded part of the stadium.
items.why: Because of + noun phrase. Because alone needs a clause.

items.s: Why not cycle to work instead ___ sitting in traffic every morning? It is cheaper, and you will get some exercise too.
items.why: Instead of + -ing.

items.s: The town is famous ___ its seafood, so make sure you try the local fish while you are there.
items.why: Famous for.

items.s: I have not heard from Sara ___ almost a month. I hope nothing has happened to her.
items.why: For + a length of time (in also works after a negative).

items.s: At first glance, the new logo looks very similar ___ the old one, but the colours are slightly brighter.
items.why: Similar to.

items.s: In addition ___ her full-time job, Rosa volunteers at an animal shelter every weekend.
items.why: In addition to + noun or -ing.

items.s: I was introduced ___ my future business partner at a friend’s wedding, of all places.
items.why: Introduce someone to someone.

items.s: Before you start the course, it helps to be familiar ___ the basic vocabulary of economics.
items.why: Familiar with something you know. (Something is familiar to you.)

items.s: The bridge, which was designed ___ a team of young engineers, has won several international awards.
items.why: By + the agent in a passive sentence.

items.s: Strong winds prevented the ferry ___ leaving the harbour, so we spent an extra night on the island.
items.why: Prevent someone / something from + -ing.

items.s: ___ to a recent survey, most teenagers spend more than four hours a day online.
items.why: According to + a source of information.

items.s: ___ from a few minor delays, the whole trip went exactly as we had planned.
items.why: Apart from means except for.

items.s: My grandmother worries ___ everything, from the weather to whether we are eating properly.
items.why: Worry about.

items.s: After two years of general medicine, Dr Khan decided to specialise ___ children’s heart conditions.
items.why: Specialise in.

items.s: The old cinema in the town centre is going to be turned ___ a modern arts centre next year.
items.why: Turn something into something: a change of form.

items.s: We had only just set off when we ran ___ some old friends we had not seen for years.
items.why: Run into (or across) someone: meet them by chance.

items.s: Some students find it hard to cope ___ the pressure of exams, so the school now offers relaxation classes.
items.why: Cope with.

items.s: The price of a ticket has gone up ___ five euros, from twenty to twenty-five.
items.why: By + the size of a change: up by five euros.

items.s: The flight was full, so we were lucky to get seats at all, let alone seats next ___ each other.
items.why: Next to.

items.s: ___ the hotel was a long way from the beach, we really enjoyed our stay there.
items.why: Although + a full clause.

items.s: The match went ahead ___ the heavy rain, and both teams played remarkably well.
items.why: Despite + a noun phrase. Although needs a clause.

items.s: Could you text me as soon ___ you land? I want to know you have arrived safely.
items.why: As soon as.

items.s: Many students take a part-time job in ___ to pay for their studies.
items.why: In order to + infinitive: purpose.

items.s: The children were not allowed to leave the table ___ everyone had finished eating.
items.why: Until gives the time when something changes.

items.s: The flat is in a great location; ___, it is far too expensive for a student like me.
items.why: However links two contrasting ideas and takes a comma.

items.s: We will miss the start of the film ___ we leave in the next five minutes.
items.why: Unless means if not.

items.s: I have emailed the museum to ask ___ students can get a discount on weekdays.
items.why: If or whether introduces an indirect yes/no question.

items.s: He walked into the meeting an hour late and sat down as ___ nothing had happened.
items.why: As though or as if + past perfect for an unreal comparison.

items.s: The course teaches practical cooking skills as ___ as the basics of nutrition.
items.why: As well as means and also.

items.s: Some of my classmates love living in the city, ___ others cannot wait to move back to the countryside.
items.why: While or whereas shows a contrast between two groups.

items.s: The guide spoke slowly and clearly ___ that everyone in the group could follow her.
items.why: So that + clause shows purpose.

items.s: Pack a warm jumper in ___ the evenings get cold. It is often windy up in the mountains.
items.why: In case + clause: as a precaution.

items.s: You are welcome to borrow my camera as ___ as you promise to look after it.
items.why: As long as means on condition that.

items.s: Make sure you book a table in advance; ___, you might not get a seat on a Saturday night.
items.why: Otherwise means if you do not.

items.s: The storm meant we could not go to the beach, so we visited the aquarium ___.
items.why: Instead at the end means in place of the thing just mentioned.

items.s: I am not going to change my mind about the job, even ___ they offer me more money.
items.why: Even if + a possible future situation.

items.s: I still cannot decide ___ to study medicine or law next year.
items.why: Whether + to-infinitive. If cannot be used here.

items.s: ___ hard I try, I can never remember people’s names at parties.
items.why: However + adjective or adverb means no matter how.

items.s: It was not ___ I got home that I realised I had left my laptop on the train.
items.why: Not until marks the point when something first happened.

items.s: The interviewer asked me ___ I had ever worked in a team before.
items.why: Reported yes/no question: if or whether.

items.s: ___ I had known how busy the restaurant would be, I would have booked a table.
items.why: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

items.s: Call me at any time ___ you need anything — even in the middle of the night.
items.why: If (or whenever) introduces the condition.

items.s: Not only did the new manager reduce costs, ___ she also improved staff morale.
items.why: Not only … but (also).

items.s: ___ the youngest of five children, Leo had to learn to stand up for himself from an early age.
items.why: As here means in the role or position of.

items.s: I had hardly closed my eyes ___ the phone started ringing.
items.why: Hardly … when (no sooner … than is the matching pair).

items.s: I wish I ___ more free time during the week; I hardly ever get to see my friends.
items.why: Wish + past simple for a present regret.

items.s: That cough sounds terrible. You ___ better see a doctor before it gets any worse.
items.why: Had better + bare infinitive: strong advice.

items.s: It was an unforgettable day for Sara. Not only ___ she win the race, but she also broke the national record.
items.why: Inversion after not only needs an auxiliary.

items.s: The kitchen window ___ broken by a football during the match last night, so it has to be replaced.
items.why: Passive, past simple: was + past participle.

items.s: By the time we finally found the cinema, the film ___ already started.
items.why: Past perfect: finished before another past action.

items.s: A new bridge has ___ built across the river to reduce traffic in the town centre.
items.why: Present perfect passive: has been + past participle.

items.s: The names of the winners will ___ announced at the end of the ceremony.
items.why: Future passive: will be + past participle.

items.s: Most teenagers hate ___ told what to do, especially by their parents.
items.why: Passive gerund: being + past participle, after verbs like hate and avoid.

items.s: I ___ not realise how late it was until I looked at my phone and saw five missed calls.
items.why: Past simple negative: did not + base verb.

items.s: Leo enjoys swimming, and so ___ his younger brother, who trains every morning before school.
items.why: So + auxiliary + subject. Enjoys → so does.

items.s: My grandfather ___ to be a fisherman before he opened his restaurant by the harbour.
items.why: Used to for past states. Would cannot be used for states like be.

items.s: It ___ have been Tom who called you this morning. He is on a plane to Brazil right now.
items.why: Cannot have + past participle: you are sure it was impossible.

items.s: I should ___ listened to my parents when they told me to start revising earlier.
items.why: Should have + past participle: a past mistake.

items.s: The restaurant was so busy yesterday that we ___ to wait an hour for a table.
items.why: The past of have to is had to. Must has no past form.

items.s: All the players ___ been asked to bring their passports, so please check that you have yours.
items.why: Present perfect passive with a plural subject: have been asked.

items.s: By this time next year, I ___ have finished my degree and started my first job.
items.why: Future perfect: will have + past participle.

items.s: Little ___ she know that her friends had organised a surprise party for her.
items.why: Negative adverbials such as little, never and hardly are followed by inversion.

items.s: The tickets sold out in less than an hour, and so ___ the extra dates they added the next day.
items.why: So + auxiliary + subject. Sold → so did.

items.s: ___ I known about the strike, I would have taken a taxi to the airport.
items.why: Had I known = If I had known. The inversion replaces if.

items.s: When we were children, our grandmother ___ tell us a story every night before bed.
items.why: Would for repeated past actions. (Used would need two words: used to tell.)

items.s: I would rather ___ go to the party if Lucy is not going to be there.
items.why: Would rather + not + base verb.

items.s: You did not need to bring a present — but it is lovely, thank you! You really should not ___.
items.why: Should not have (brought it): the participle is left out because it is clear.

items.s: The student ___ sits next to me in maths has just moved here from Canada.
items.why: Who (or that) for people as the subject.

items.s: We had a long chat with a neighbour ___ son plays for the national team.
items.why: Whose shows possession.

items.s: Sintra is the town ___ my parents first met, so we go back there every summer.
items.why: Where for places, when a full clause follows.

items.s: Our flight was cancelled at the last minute, ___ meant we had to spend the night at the airport.
items.why: Which after a comma refers back to the whole idea before it.

items.s: I will never forget the day ___ I passed my driving test. I drove around for hours!
items.why: When for times.

items.s: Nobody showed Tom how to play the guitar; he taught ___ by watching videos online.
items.why: Reflexive pronoun: the subject and the object are the same person.

items.s: Did you two enjoy ___ at the festival? You both look exhausted!
items.why: Enjoy + reflexive pronoun. You two → yourselves.

items.s: Although they live on opposite sides of the world, the two cousins speak to each ___ every day.
items.why: Each other: a reciprocal pronoun.

items.s: ___ is often said that first impressions are the ones that count.
items.why: It is said that … : it stands for the that-clause.

items.s: ___ used to be a cinema on this corner, but it closed down when I was a child.
items.why: There + be introduces something that existed.

items.s: My laptop finally stopped working last week, so I have had to buy a new ___.
items.why: One replaces a countable noun when it is a different thing.

items.s: The museum, ___ opened in 1998, attracts thousands of visitors every year.
items.why: After a comma (non-defining clause) use which, not that.

items.s: The receptionist to ___ I spoke was extremely helpful and found us a better room.
items.why: Preposition + whom for people.

items.s: ___ surprised me most about the city was how friendly everyone was.
items.why: What means the thing that.

items.s: I felt so ill that I did not eat ___ for the whole day.
items.why: Anything in negative sentences. Nothing would make a double negative.

items.s: Group projects are popular with students because they allow ___ to learn from each other.
items.why: Object pronoun after allow.

items.s: The city is famous for ___ ancient walls, which were built by the Romans.
items.why: Its, with no apostrophe, is the possessive of it.

items.s: I find ___ difficult to concentrate when there is music playing in the background.
items.why: Find it + adjective + to-infinitive: it stands for the infinitive.

items.s: Of all the films I saw this year, the ___ I enjoyed most was a small Iranian drama.
items.why: The one = the film.

items.s: Nobody really knows ___ happened to the ship after it left the harbour in 1872.
items.why: What = the thing that.

items.s: Now that she is eighteen, Ana would love a flat of her ___.
items.why: Of your own.

items.s: Anyone ___ wants to join the trip should sign up by Friday.
items.why: Anyone who … : who for people.

items.s: I would appreciate ___ if you could reply by the end of the week.
items.why: Appreciate it if … : it stands for the if-clause.

items.s: Many of the people ___ I interviewed had never travelled abroad.
items.why: Object of the relative clause: whom, who or that.

items.s: Can you get some milk on your way home? There is not ___ left in the fridge.
items.why: Not any: any in negatives. Milk is uncountable.

items.s: Very ___ people turned up to the meeting, so it was postponed until next week.
items.why: Very few + countable noun: almost none.

items.s: We do not have ___ time left, so let us focus on the most important points.
items.why: Much with uncountable nouns in negatives.

items.s: I tried both of the shortcuts you suggested, but ___ of them worked.
items.why: Neither is for two things.

items.s: I invited six friends to my party, but ___ of them could come, so I celebrated with my family instead.
items.why: None is for more than two.

items.s: At sixteen, you are not old ___ to vote, but you can get a part-time job.
items.why: Enough comes after the adjective.

items.s: We visited four countries in two weeks, and ___ one was completely different from the last.
items.why: Each or every + one, for the members of a group taken separately.

items.s: We have not quite finished the exercise. Could we have ___ ten minutes, please?
items.why: Another + number + plural noun means that many more.

items.s: Some people relax by doing sport, while ___ prefer to read or watch films.
items.why: Others means other people. No noun follows.

items.s: I have two brothers, and ___ of them work in IT, like my father.
items.why: Both of + plural pronoun, for two people.

items.s: I spent the ___ weekend revising for my biology exam, so I did not go out once.
items.why: The whole + singular noun.

items.s: It rained ___ day yesterday, so we stayed indoors and played board games.
items.why: All day means from morning to night.

items.s: Who would you say is ___ best player in your team at the moment?
items.why: The before a superlative.

items.s: Hardly ___ students signed up for the trip, so the school had to cancel it.
items.why: Hardly any means almost none.

items.s: There is not ___ point in complaining now; the decision has already been made.
items.why: Not much or not any with uncountable nouns.

items.s: I have made ___ few friends since I moved here, so I do not feel lonely any more.
items.why: A few is positive (some). Few alone is negative (hardly any).

items.s: ___ four years, the Olympic Games are held in a different country.
items.why: Every + number + plural noun for regular intervals.

items.s: I have ___ idea where I left my keys. Have you seen them anywhere?
items.why: No idea. Not and none cannot go directly before a noun.

items.s: The buses run ___ twenty minutes during the week, but less often at weekends.
items.why: Every + number + plural noun for regular intervals.

items.s: After ___ the effort she had put into her project, she deserved to win first prize.
items.why: All the + noun.

items.s: Most ___ the people I spoke to at the conference had travelled from abroad.
items.why: Most of the + plural noun.

items.s: Once ___ week, the whole family gets together for lunch at my grandmother’s house.
items.why: Once a week: a means each here.

items.s: The two teams scored three goals ___, so the match went to penalties.
items.why: Each after a number: three goals for every team.

items.s: There is ___ doubt that the internet has changed the way we learn.
items.why: There is no doubt that … .

items.s: Martin was ___ tired after the night shift that he fell asleep on the bus home.
items.why: So + adjective + that + result.

items.s: It was ___ a beautiful evening that we decided to eat outside.
items.why: Such + a + adjective + noun + that + result.

items.s: I was far ___ shocked by the news to say anything at all.
items.why: Too + adjective + to-infinitive.

items.s: The concert was far better ___ any of us had expected.
items.why: Comparative + than. Watch the spelling: than, not then.

items.s: My new phone is not nearly as fast ___ my old one was, which is really frustrating.
items.why: Not (nearly) as + adjective + as.

items.s: The more you practise speaking, ___ more confident you will feel in the exam.
items.why: The + comparative, the + comparative.

items.s: The longer we waited for news, the ___ anxious we became.
items.why: The + comparative, the + comparative. Anxious takes more.

items.s: This is by far the ___ challenging course I have ever taken.
items.why: By far + superlative.

items.s: The new model is ___ more expensive than the old one, but it is also much faster.
items.why: Much, far, even or still can strengthen a comparative. Very cannot.

items.s: No sooner had we sat down at our table ___ the waiter brought us the menu.
items.why: No sooner … than. Hardly … when is the matching pair.

items.s: Doctors recommend that we eat ___ sugar and more vegetables.
items.why: Less with uncountable nouns. Fewer is for countable nouns.

items.s: There were so ___ people at the concert that we could hardly move.
items.why: So many + countable noun + that + result.

items.s: The film was so long ___ half the audience had fallen asleep before the end.
items.why: So + adjective + that + result.

items.s: Try to get here as early ___ you can — the best seats go very quickly.
items.why: As + adverb + as you can.

items.s: It took me a while, but I eventually got used ___ driving on the left.
items.why: Get used to + -ing.

items.s: To be honest, I would rather stay at home ___ go out in this weather.
items.why: Would rather … than.

items.s: As far ___ I am concerned, the new timetable is a big improvement.
items.why: As far as I am concerned: in my opinion.

items.s: Maria has been working at the hospital ___ she finished her degree in 2019.
items.why: Since + the starting point, with the present perfect.

items.s: I am sure he did not break your phone ___ purpose; it just slipped out of his hand.
items.why: On purpose = deliberately.

items.s: Could you look ___ my cat while I am on holiday? She only needs feeding twice a day.
items.why: Look after = take care of.

items.s: The outdoor concert was called ___ at the last minute because of a storm warning.
items.why: Call off = cancel.

items.s: She grew ___ in a small fishing village, which is why she still loves the sea.
items.why: Grow up.

items.s: We ran ___ of petrol on the motorway and had to walk two kilometres to a garage.
items.why: Run out of = have none left.

items.s: We set ___ at dawn so that we would reach the top of the mountain before midday.
items.why: Set off (or out) = start a journey.

items.s: Scientists have carried ___ a series of tests on the new vaccine, and the results are promising.
items.why: Carry out tests, research, a survey.

items.s: Although the forecast was terrible, the weather turned ___ to be perfect for our picnic.
items.why: Turn out to be = prove to be in the end.

items.s: After years of trying, my uncle finally managed to give ___ smoking.
items.why: Give up = stop doing.

items.s: While tidying the attic, I came ___ some old photos of my grandparents’ wedding.
items.why: Come across = find by chance.

items.s: Could you find ___ what time the museum opens on Sundays?
items.why: Find out = discover information.

items.s: If you keep spending money like that, you will end ___ with nothing left by the end of the month.
items.why: End up = find yourself in a situation at the end.

items.s: The manager promised to deal ___ our complaint as soon as possible.
items.why: Deal with.

items.s: I get ___ really well with my new flatmates, which makes sharing a kitchen much easier.
items.why: Get on (or along) with someone.

items.s: Nothing can make ___ for all the time we lost while the train was delayed.
items.why: Make up for = compensate for.

items.s: I cannot put up ___ this noise any longer — I am going to speak to the neighbours.
items.why: Put up with = tolerate.

items.s: The train is quicker. ___ the other hand, the bus is much cheaper.
items.why: On the other hand introduces the opposite point.

items.s: We talked about going away for the weekend, but in the ___ we decided to stay at home.
items.why: In the end = finally, after some time.

items.s: ___ first, I found the city overwhelming, but after a few weeks I felt completely at home.
items.why: At first = in the beginning (before a change).

items.s: The factory closed last year. ___ a result, hundreds of people lost their jobs.
items.why: As a result.

items.s: There were a few problems with the hotel, but ___ the whole we had a wonderful holiday.
items.why: On the whole = generally.

items.s: ___ the way, did you remember to buy the tickets for Saturday?
items.why: By the way introduces a new topic.

items.s: I cannot come to the party. I have too much work and, ___ any case, I do not really feel well.
items.why: In any case = anyway.

items.s: You are welcome to stay with us ___ the time being, until you find a flat of your own.
items.why: For the time being = for now.

items.s: Your table will be ready in about ten minutes. ___ the meantime, can I get you something to drink?
items.why: In the meantime = while you wait.

items.s: Some birds, ___ instance, can sleep while they are flying.
items.why: For instance = for example.

items.s: I am so sorry about your vase. I knocked it over ___ accident when I was cleaning.
items.why: By accident = not on purpose.

items.s: The students were made ___ rewrite the whole essay because they had copied it from the internet.
items.why: Passive of make takes a to-infinitive.

items.s: My brother suggested ___ we should leave early to avoid the traffic.
items.why: Suggest that + clause (never suggest to do).

items.s: She finally admitted that it ___ been her who broke the window.
items.why: Reported past: it had been her.

items.s: The new president is said ___ be very popular with young voters.
items.why: Be said to + infinitive.

items.s: My parents have always encouraged me ___ follow my dreams, even when they seemed unrealistic.
items.why: Encourage someone to do something.

items.s: He promised me ___ he would never be late again — but he was late the very next day.
items.why: Promise (someone) that + clause.

items.s: We left very early so ___ not to get stuck in the rush-hour traffic.
items.why: So as not to + infinitive: negative purpose.

items.s: Please do not hesitate ___ contact me if you have any questions.
items.why: Hesitate to do something.

items.s: Personally, I prefer spending time outdoors ___ sitting in front of a screen.
items.why: Prefer A to B.

items.s: Even though we offered to split the bill, he insisted ___ paying for everyone.
items.why: Insist on + -ing.

items.s: The room had nothing ___ a small bed and a broken lamp, so we left the next morning.
items.why: Nothing but = only.

items.s: The trip was ___ from perfect: it rained every day and our luggage got lost.
items.why: Far from perfect = not at all perfect.

items.s: I did not enjoy the film ___ all; in fact, I left before the end.
items.why: Not … at all = not in any way.

items.s: Do not worry about the money. You can pay me back ___ you like — there is no hurry.
items.why: Whenever = at any time.

items.s: She told us she had never been abroad, ___ surprised everyone in the class.
items.why: Which after a comma refers back to the whole idea.

items.s: The village, ___ can only be reached by boat, has fewer than a hundred inhabitants.
items.why: Non-defining clause about a thing: which, never that.

items.s: The main reason for ___ I chose this university was its excellent library.
items.why: Preposition + which for things.

items.s: We stayed in a small hotel, the owner of ___ was a retired chef.
items.why: The owner of which = whose owner.

items.s: ___ I like most about living by the sea is the fresh air in the morning.
items.why: What = the thing that.

items.s: I cannot believe ___ a mess the children have made of the kitchen!
items.why: What + a + noun in exclamations.

items.s: No matter ___ you decide, I will support you.
items.why: No matter what = whatever.

items.s: Will the weather be good enough for the picnic? I hope ___ — we have already bought all the food.
items.why: I hope so: so replaces the clause.

items.s: I have ___ much homework this week that I have not had time to go out at all.
items.why: So much + uncountable noun + that.

items.s: Is this ___ first time you have been to Lisbon? You seem to know your way around.
items.why: The first time + present perfect.

items.s: ___ older I get, the more I appreciate my parents’ advice.
items.why: The + comparative, the + comparative.

items.s: Regular exercise is ___ of the best ways to reduce stress.
items.why: One of the + superlative + plural noun.

items.s: Thank you for ___ your help with the move; I could not have done it without you.
items.why: All + possessive + noun.

items.s: What ___ beautiful view! I could sit here for hours.
items.why: What a + adjective + singular noun.

items.s: She burst ___ tears when she heard that she had won the scholarship.
items.why: Burst into tears / laughter.

items.s: Digital cameras have changed photography completely. ___ allow photographers to see their results instantly.
items.why: A plural noun (digital cameras) is picked up by they or these.

items.s: With a digital camera you can see every photo the moment you take it. ___ means that mistakes can be corrected immediately.
items.why: This sums up the whole idea before it: seeing every photo at once.

items.s: Our school started a volunteering club last year, and ___ now meets every Friday after lessons.
items.why: A singular noun (the club) is picked up by it.

items.s: Members visit a care home in the village, where ___ help the residents with their shopping.
items.why: Subject of help: the members become they.

items.s: The members bring games and cakes every week, and the residents say ___ visits are the best part of their week.
